questions.prompt: What does Flint notice when he looks up from his finished map?
choices: The forest looks different from his map.
Everyone is waiting to praise his map.
The map has disappeared from his hands.
questions.answer: The forest looks different from his map.
questions.evidenceText: The forest around him looked very different to the forest on his map.

questions.prompt: Why is Flint's beautiful first map already wrong?
choices: Rain had washed away the ink.
Pip had drawn extra paths on it.

questions.prompt: What does Flint's choice to start another map show?
choices: He can enjoy the work even when the forest changes.
He expects his second map to stay correct forever.
He keeps mapping only so he will never get lost.
questions.answer: He can enjoy the work even when the forest changes.
questions.rationale: Flint is not upset when he starts a new map, and later he is already very happy as the paths rearrange; this shows he can enjoy the mapping work even when the forest changes.
questions.evidenceText: Flint took out a new piece of parchment. "I'll make another one," he said. He was not upset about this.

supportingEvidence.evidenceText: Then Flint started on the next map. He was already very happy. Outside, the paths rearranged themselves quietly.
